task.brief: Investigate process_file at /process/file in this Open WebUI revision. Trace the caller, the supplied file_id and the destination collection_name through authorization and the eventual processing or vector write. Explain whether the object authorized for input and the object affected by output are the same, and what happens for caller-owned versus another user's file. Do not assume the caller owns the destination collection. Give visible conditions and specific remaining limits; this is behavior investigation.

behavior.explanation: The route requires a verified user and authorizes the input File record by role/ownership: admins may load any file ID, while non-admins only load a file whose user_id equals the caller's ID. Once a file is loaded, process_file does not validate write access to a caller-supplied collection_name. It can therefore process an authorized input file and target a separately named vector collection without establishing that the caller owns or may write that destination. The default destination is derived as file-{file.id}, but it remains a vector collection distinct from the File database object. Actual output varies with content, destination presence, bypass configuration, existing collection state, duplicate detection, and processing errors.

branches.condition: Request reaches POST /api/v1/retrieval/process/file with a caller accepted by get_verified_user.
branches.explanation: The retrieval router is mounted at /api/v1/retrieval, the handler is POST /process/file, and its dependency is get_verified_user. The visible authentication code rejects requests with no bearer/cookie/middleware token with 401. The complete verified-user role check was not read.

branches.condition: Caller is not admin and supplied file_id identifies a File with user_id equal to caller user.id.
branches.explanation: process_file calls get_file_by_id_and_user_id(file_id, user.id). That model query filters simultaneously by id and user_id, so an owned file is loaded and processing proceeds.

branches.condition: Caller is not admin and supplied file_id belongs to another user.
branches.explanation: The id-and-user query returns no file when ownership does not match, so the guarded if file processing body—including content extraction, file updates, embedding, and vector insertion—is not entered. The exact final HTTP status/detail is outside the successfully read range.

branches.condition: Caller role equals admin and supplied file_id exists, including when owned by another user.
branches.explanation: Admins use get_file_by_id(file_id) with no user_id filter. Thus an admin can process another user's file; emitted document metadata still records created_by as the file's user_id, and successful processing updates that same File record.

branches.condition: No collection_name is supplied and embedding/retrieval bypass is disabled.
branches.explanation: The destination is set to file-{file.id}. save_docs_to_vector_db receives metadata including that file_id and the computed content hash. Because add is false when no collection_name was supplied, an already-existing destination collection causes an early successful return without inserting new vectors; otherwise embeddings are generated and items are inserted into file-{file.id}. On success, the File record is updated with meta.collection_name, data.status=completed, and the hash.

branches.condition: A non-null collection_name is supplied and the input file passed the file authorization check.
branches.explanation: process_file passes the supplied name directly to save_docs_to_vector_db and sets add=true. There is no call in this handler to _validate_collection_access, even though that helper exists and other processing endpoints visibly invoke it for write access. The vector helper checks/queries/inserts by the supplied collection name but performs no visible principal-to-collection authorization. Therefore the source-visible path does not establish that the caller owns or has write permission to the destination collection.

branches.condition: A supplied collection_name already exists, bypass is disabled, and no earlier duplicate/error condition aborts.
branches.explanation: Because add=true for every supplied collection_name, existence does not trigger the add=false early return; generated items are inserted into the existing named collection. Destination ownership is not checked in the visible path.

branches.condition: form_data.content is truthy.
branches.explanation:
The caller-provided content replaces
with newlines, is stored as the file's content, and becomes the document body. Beforeward, the handler attempts to delete the default file-{file.id} collection and ignores any deletion exception—even when a different custom destination was supplied. It then writes to the selected default or supplied destination unless bypassed or an error occurs.

branches.condition: No content override is supplied, but collection_name is supplied.
branches.explanation: The handler first queries the default file-{file.id} collection filtered by file_id and copies those documents/metadata if found; otherwise it constructs a document from file.data.content. Those documents are then targeted to the caller-supplied collection.

branches.condition: Neither content nor collection_name is supplied.
branches.explanation: The authorized File's stored path is loaded and parsed when present; otherwise file.data.content is used. Document metadata binds the content to file.id and records created_by=file.user_id. The resulting text is written back to the File record before vector processing.

branches.condition: BYPASS_EMBEDDING_AND_RETRIEVAL is true after the file and text have been prepared.
branches.explanation: No vector write occurs. The handler still updates the authorized File's content, status to completed, and hash, then returns collection_name null.

branches.condition: The selected destination already contains the same hash and the first matching metadata file_id differs from the current file_id.
branches.explanation: save_docs_to_vector_db raises DUPLICATE_CONTENT. If the matching file_id is the same, it is treated as a re-add/reindex and this duplicate check does not block; later collection-state behavior still applies.

branches.condition: Comparing the object authorized at input with objects affected by output.
branches.explanation: They are not generally the same authorization object. Input authorization is against a relational File row keyed by file_id and, for non-admins, user_id. Outputs include mutations to that same File row plus insertion into a vector collection keyed only by collection_name. With no supplied destination, file-{file.id} creates a naming relationship but not object identity or a separate collection authorization check. With a supplied destination, the destination can be entirely independent of the authorized File.

missing.detail: The lines immediately after process_file's visible exception block and the final no-file branch were not successfully read, so the exact HTTP status/detail returned for a missing or unauthorized file, and precise exception mapping for processing/vector failures, remain unverified.

Comments identify intended callers such as /files/, /files/{file_id}/data/content/update, and knowledge file add/update, but their actual call sites and any path-specific upstream checks were not successfully traced. Direct access to the retrieval endpoint is nevertheless source-visible and protected by get_verified_user plus the handler's own file lookup.

They may change whether a vector effect occurs, but no additional destination authorization is visible in the traced handler/helper.
